objectives: Recognise rimes in taught bl-words while keeping the initial blend intact.
Group words that share the same vowel and ending sounds.
Distinguish similar bl-words by checking the vowel and final consonant.
Read each word fully rather than relying on the rime alone.
concepts: A word family groups words with a shared rime.
Words in a family can have different onsets but share the vowel and ending.
The initial blend bl stays /b/ /l/; the rime changes across blob, blip, blot, black and block.
A word-family sort is a decoding aid, not permission to guess.

definitions.definition: A group of words that share a rime, such as blob and sob with -ob.
The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
The initial consonant or consonant group before the vowel.
Compare two words to notice a sound or spelling difference.

workedExamples.solution: Both share -ob; blob has onset bl and sob has onset s.
Both share -ock, though their onsets are different.
Both begin bl, but black has -ack and block has -ock.
Blip has the rime -ip; blob and blot have different rimes.

commonMistakes: Grouping words because they share the first letter instead of the rime.
Treating black and block as the same family because both begin bl.
Ignoring the final consonant when comparing blob and blot.
Guessing a word from the family label without decoding it.
keyTakeaways: Compare the vowel and ending to identify a rime.
Words can share a rime while having different onsets.
Black and block share bl but have different rimes.
Always decode the full word after sorting.
revisionPoints: block and sock share -ock; black has -ack.

basic.prompt: What is the rime in black?

conceptual.prompt: What makes blob and sob members of the same word family?
Do black and block share the same rime?
conceptual.answer: No; black has -ack and block has -ock.

conceptual.prompt: Why is rime sorting not the same as guessing?
conceptual.answer: The reader must still decode every grapheme in the full word.

application.prompt: Which word belongs with block and sock by rime?
Which word belongs with blip and lip?

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How are blob and blot alike and different?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Both begin bl, but their rimes are -ob and -ot.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why can black and block be placed in different rime groups?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Their vowels differ: short a in black and short o in block.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What should you do if a word fits a rime group but does not sound right?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Decode it again and check every sound.

mixedReview.prompt: What is the onset in blip?
What does a word-family sort help you notice?
mixedReview.answer: Shared rimes and differences among words

activities.name: Sort words into rime families.
steps: Read blob, sob, blip, lip, blot, hot, black, block and sock.
Group words by the vowel and ending sounds.
Name the rime in each group.
Read each word again to confirm the sort.

activities.name: Compare near-neighbour bl-words.
steps: Place blob beside blot and black beside block.
Say the onset and rime for each word.
Identify the sound or spelling that changes.
Explain why the full word must still be decoded.

outcomes: Identify the onset and rime in taught bl-words.
Group words accurately by shared rime.
Explain how words with the same onset can have different rimes.
Decode every word after completing a word-family sort.
